children.text: Key Takeaways
Colorado sets DWAI at 0.05 percent BAC and DUI at 0.08 percent BAC, and police can arrest below 0.05 percent when impairment appears.
Drivers in injury crashes must stop, remain at the scene, and meet legal duties under CRS 42-4-1601.
After a drunk driving accident, call 911, get medical care, document the scene, and have the police record suspected impairment.
An injured person can sue a drunk driver in civil court by proving negligence caused the crash, even if criminal charges are filed.
Most Colorado injury claims carry a two-year deadline, and courts may award exemplary damages for reckless conduct.

A drunk driving accident can turn an ordinary Colorado commute into a crisis filled with physical pain, financial strain, and urgent legal questions, especially when the at-fault driver faces criminal charges. During these moments, a
drunk driving accident lawyer
can help victims protect their rights, preserve critical evidence, and build a strong claim grounded in Colorado law.

Knowing what steps to take immediately after a crash can protect both your health and your legal rights. Taking a few immediate steps can make a significant difference. Call 911, seek medical attention for any injuries, and make sure law enforcement documents suspected impairment in an official crash report. Next, exchange contact and insurance details, photograph vehicle damage, and preserve witness information whenever possible. Finally, contact a personal injury attorney quickly to manage insurance negotiations, comply with Colorado’s two-year statute of limitations for most injury claims, and pursue full financial recovery.

Colorado Drunk Driving Laws
Colorado enforces clear standards for alcohol-related driving offenses, and those limits often shape civil liability after a drunk driving accident. According to the
Colorado Department of Transportation

, drivers may face DWAI (Driving While Ability Impaired) charges at a 0.05 percent blood alcohol concentration, or BAC, which refers to the amount of alcohol present in a person’s bloodstream. A more serious offense, DUI (Driving Under the Influence), generally applies when a driver reaches a 0.08 percent BAC or higher. Even when a driver’s BAC falls below 0.05 percent, law enforcement may still make an arrest if officers observe clear signs of impairment.

These thresholds demonstrate how even small amounts of alcohol can affect judgment and driving ability, which often becomes important when proving negligence in a Colorado civil injury case. Colorado law also allows arrest below 0.05 percent when observable impairment exists. The only absolute way to ensure lawful and safe driving is to maintain a blood alcohol concentration of zero.
Benefits of Hiring a Lawyer for a Drunk Driving Accident
While prosecutors pursue criminal penalties, a civil claim focuses on restoring financial stability, and working with a
drunk driving accident lawyer

allows injured victims to pursue compensation without absorbing every legal burden alone. Insurance carriers frequently minimize payouts in DUI crash cases by disputing injury severity or suggesting shared fault, yet legal counsel pushes back with evidence and negotiation leverage grounded in
Colorado negligence law
Helping You to Receive the Compensation You Deserve

Because strong legal representation focuses on maximizing recovery, a drunk driving accident often produces long-term medical complications and lost income, which makes a comprehensive damages calculation essential. We build claims through detailed documentation and strategic negotiation, presenting clear proof of economic and non-economic harm in order to seek meaningful recovery.
Before entering settlement discussions, careful evaluation should include:
Medical Expenses:
Emergency treatment, hospitalization, surgery, physical therapy, medication, and projected future care costs.
Lost Wages:
Income missed during recovery and diminished earning capacity when injuries limit future employment.
Pain and Suffering:
Physical discomfort, emotional trauma, and lifestyle disruption tied directly to the DUI crash.
By connecting each category of loss to the impaired driver’s conduct, a
drunk driving accident lawyer
strengthens the claim and positions the case for trial when negotiations stall.
Relieving You of Financial Burden

As medical bills accumulate and insurers request statements, legal pressure intensifies, which makes professional advocacy invaluable after a drunk driving accident. A trial-ready legal team manages communication with insurance adjusters, gathers accident reconstruction evidence, and coordinates medical documentation so injured clients can focus on recovery rather than paperwork.
Because contingency fee arrangements shift financial risk away from families, representation from a
drunk driving accident lawyer
allows victims to pursue justice without upfront legal costs.
Preventing a Dismissal if Your Case Goes to Trial

Although many DUI crash claims resolve through settlement, thorough trial preparation protects against procedural setbacks. Defense counsel may challenge causation, argue comparative fault, or file motions seeking dismissal based on technical grounds, and strategic preparation prevents those tactics from undermining a valid claim.
By complying with Colorado civil procedure rules and preserving critical evidence, legal representation strengthens the case foundation and supports a compelling presentation before a judge or jury.
Steps to Take After a Drunk Driving Accident

In the chaotic aftermath of a crash involving suspected impairment, immediate action protects both safety and legal rights, and Colorado law places clear responsibilities on every driver involved in an injury collision.
As explained in the
Colorado Revised Statutes section 42-4-1601

, a driver directly involved in an accident resulting in injury or death must immediately stop at the scene, or as close to the scene as possible, and remain there until all statutory obligations are fulfilled, reinforcing accountability after a serious collision.
To protect your health and preserve a strong civil claim after a drunk driving accident, take the following steps:
Call Law Enforcement:
Request officers at the scene so suspected impairment, witness statements, and crash details become part of the official record. That report becomes key evidence later, and you can
get a copy of the police report in Denver
within a few business days of the crash.
Seek Immediate Medical Care:
Prompt treatment documents injuries and prevents insurance companies from later disputing causation.
Exchange Required Information:
Provide and obtain names, contact details, registration, and insurance information as required by Colorado law.
Document the Scene:
Photograph vehicle damage, skid marks, debris patterns, and visible injuries before vehicles move when possible.
Consult Legal Counsel Quickly
Speaking with a DUI accident attorney early helps protect evidence, manage insurance communications, and safeguard compliance with filing deadlines.
These steps strengthen a civil case from the outset and limit opportunities for insurers to downplay the seriousness of a drunk driving accident claim.
Your Legal Options After Being Hit by a Drunk Driver
After a drunk
driving accident in Colorado

, victims have legal options to pursue accountability and financial recovery. While prosecutors may bring criminal charges against the impaired driver, injured individuals also have the right to seek compensation through the civil justice system.

One option involves filing a personal injury claim against the intoxicated driver whose negligence caused the crash. Through this civil claim, victims may pursue compensation for medical expenses, lost income, and the physical and emotional harm caused by the collision.

Another legal option may involve seeking exemplary damages when the driver’s conduct shows willful or reckless disregard for the safety of others. Because driving under the influence often meets that standard, Colorado courts may allow additional damages in a lawsuit arising from a drunk driving accident.
